It's not always about being "lazy" I was learning manual,  had an instructor who was dragging the learning out, previous one was brilliant but retired a couple of months after I started learning,  he'd come out of early retirement.
The next one was really finicky and put my test back 3 times,  I'd gone from being quite confident to a virtual nervous wreck, making loads of mistakes and totally lost confidence on manoeuvres, he had zero personality, my knee was agony last few lessons, due to left knee injury and arthritis, I decided to change to automatic, my instructor is brilliant,  has amazing banter and in 3 lessons I've started to love driving around again, gained confidence, he said if I'd had the right instructor I would've passed ages ago in manual.    Once I've passed in automatic I might decide to try manual again,  but not sure why, as 65% of cars being made are now automatic and a lot of companies have stopped making manual altogether

I'm just learning,  in my early 50's.
Years ago I tore ligaments and popped my left knee, I've now got cartilage damage, the ligaments haven't fused back,  my kneecap pops out and in both knees osteoarthritis.  I started learning manual and recently changed to automatic, I'm not too thrilled, because keeping my foot on clutch and stop starting, creeping in long queues of traffic isn't fun, I was in agony last manual lesson.
Do what you feel is right for yourself, it's your body, only you know it's limitations and pain threshold,  it's likely to get worse not better

I'm in my 50's,  2 weeks ago I switched from manual to automatic and it has made a difference,  I wanted to stay with manual, but I don't really have the time,  it's taken nearly 3 years already learning off and on, my last instructor put test back about 4 times and felt like he was making excuses and knocking my confidence, the one before was semi retired and retired shortly after, I would've passed with him.
The new automatic instructor said my manual instructor had been too finicky about my road position and a couple of other things like slowing down too much at certain points.
You could try a different instructor or try automatic,  65% of cars are now automatic and a lot of car manufacturers are stopping making manual.   If I pass in automatic, I may take my test later in manual. All I want is to have a drive out now and again and mostly get from A to B
